newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products all fall, mogas tumbles $5-$6.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products all fall, mogas tumbles $5-$6.

text.p: NWE oil products all fell on Monday morning after crude oil futures' late slump on Friday, with gasoline the weakest product, dealers said.

Eurograde gasoline barges were quoted at $189/$191 fob Rotterdam by late morning, $5 lower than late session on Friday. Early on, one trading house sold two barges at $189 fob AR and $188 fob ARA, the latter some $10 below Friday's weakest deal.
As July approached, the June/July swap level came in to around $5 a tonne.
"There's ample supply, tanks are full and prompt is steadily going to weaken to bring that (June/July) spread down to zero," one trader said.
Heating oil barges were down $3/$4 in line with IPE June gas oil futures weakness. The fall persuaded buyers to stay away for the time being, particularly after reasonable buying on Friday.
German buyers were still discouraged by persistent weakness of the mark against the dollar.
Fuel oil barges traded once at $86 fob Rotterdam. The subsequent bid-offer range -- $85/$86 -- changed little through the morning. Initial bunker demand was thin.
